svg.title: An agent is a loop the model decides to leave
svg.desc: A hand-drawn whiteboard with three stacked panels: one call runs prompt to model to answer in a straight line, a chain runs through three model calls still in a straight line, and an agent is drawn as a genuine cycle from model to tool call to run it to observation and back, with a single dashed exit arrow labelled stop? and the word agent circled. A fourth panel reading 'just let it run until it's done' is struck through. To the right, a chart shows end-to-end success falling along the 95-percent-per-step curve from 95 at one step to 59.9 at ten - ringed with 0.95^10 = 0.60 written in - against a dashed 99-percent curve that reaches 90.4.
svg.text: An agent is a loop the model decides to leave
one call - control flow is yours
chain - still yours: you wrote the order
when to exit. That is the
just let it run until it's done
95% per step is a GOOD agent
...and then? the loop must be BOUNDED
